comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 beer & wine license for existing restaurant in the CCB district at 653 Clay St, 44 meters away on the same block. Agency referral for continuation of existing restaurant use, approved in 28 days.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved Type 41 for an existing restaurant in CCB as a continuation of use without conditions or a hearing. This agency referral shows the department treats beer-and-wine service as permitted in conjunction with an established restaurant in the CCB district.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: DPH restaurant referral for the same 653 Clay St address (44m away) in CCB, approved 23 days after filing. Confirms continuation of existing restaurant use under Planning Code Section 810.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning's approval language ('conditionally permitted in the C-C-B Zoning District per PC Section 810. Continuation of existing use') confirms that established restaurants in CCB may continue operating without triggering a new conditional use process for routine permits.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant approval at 660 Sacramento St in CCB, only 13 meters away, approved in 17 days. Planning cited prior Building Permit 9021345 establishing the use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral demonstrates that Planning approves continuation of previously established restaurant uses in CCB by administrative review, relying on prior building permits to confirm the legal status, with no hearing or conditions.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant (d.b.a. Neutral) at 683 Commercial St in CCB, 12 meters away on the same block, approved in 29 days. Same zoning district and immediate vicinity.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved this limited restaurant as principally permitted in CCB per Section 810.43 through an agency referral with no conditions, showing that restaurant continuations on this block proceed administratively.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 47 and 58 full-bar licenses for existing restaurant at 653 Commercial St in CCB, 21 meters away, approved in 27 days. Same block, same district, higher-level alcohol license.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved even a Type 47 full-bar license in CCB at this address as a continuation of existing conditional use, citing Section 810.44 and 178. If full liquor was approved as a continuation, beer-and-wine (Type 41) at an established restaurant will follow the same path.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 for restaurant at 550 Kearny St in C-3-O district, 68 meters away, approved in 19 days. Continuation of existing restaurant use with beer and wine service.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This C-3-O approval (an adjacent downtown district) for Type 41 as continuation of existing use took under three weeks and had no conditions, showing the administrative path for adding beer and wine to an established restaurant in this area.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 for restaurant (K Five Fifty) at 550 Kearny St in C-3-O, 68m away, approved in 5 days. Fast approval for beer and wine at a restaurant near Chinatown.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved this Type 41 in five working days as principally permitted in C-3-O. The record shows no concerns about the high density of licenses in the area, and the quick turnaround signals that continuation-of-use alcohol referrals are routine.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant continuation at 600 Kearny St in CCB, 40 meters away, approved in 9 days. Same zoning district, same block, DPH health referral approved quickly.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This nine-day approval for a limited-restaurant continuation in CCB shows Planning treats routine health and ABC referrals for existing restaurants as ministerial; no conditions were imposed.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health-Restaurant application at 801 Kearny St in CCB, 195m away, denied after three years. Only denial in the candidate set; took from June 2016 to August 2019.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This is the only denial among CCB restaurant applications in the area. The record gives no stated reason for the denial, and the three-year timeline suggests the applicant may have failed to complete requirements or the use was never legally established, not that Planning denied continuation of a lawful restaurant.

conditions: Overhead Wiring: The Property owner will allow MUNI to inst all eyebolts in the building adjacent to its electric streetcar line to support its overhead wire system if requested by MUNI or MTA.

SFMTA has final authority on the type, placement and number of Class 2 bicycle racks within the public ROW. Prior to issuance of first architectural addenda, the project sponsor shall contact the SFMTA Bike Parking Program at bikeparking@sfmta.com to coordinate the installation of on-street bicycle racks and ensure that the proposed bicycle racks meet the SFMTA’s bicycle parking guidelines.

Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an applicati on for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay. (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. Design – Compliance at Plan Stage (standard)

Final Materials: The Project Sponsor shall continue to work with Planning Department on the building design. Final materials, glazing, color, texture, landscaping, and detailing shall be subject to Department staff review and approval. The architectural addenda shall be reviewed and approved by the Planning Department prior to issuance. (standard)

Garbage, Composting and Recycling Storage: Space for the collection and storage of garbage, composting, and recycling shall be provided within enclosed areas on the property and clearly labeled and illustrated on the building permit plans. Space for the collection and storage of recyclable and compostable materials that meets the size, location, accessibility and other standards specified by the San Francisco Recycling Program shall be provided at the ground level of the buildings. (standard)

Rooftop Mechanical Equipment: Pursuant to Planning Code 141, the Project Sponsor shall submit a roof plan to the Planning Department prior to Planning approval of the building permit application. Rooftop mechanical equipment, if any is proposed as part of the Project, is required to be screened so as not to be visible from any point at or below the roof level of the subject building. (standard)
Noise: Plans submitted with the building permit applicatio n for the approved project shall incorporate acoustical insulation and other sound proofing measures to control noise. (standard)

Odor Control Unit: In order to ensure any significant noxious or offensive odors are prevented from escaping the premises once the project is operational, the building permit application to implement the project shall include air cleaning or odor control equipment details and manufacturer specifications on the plans. Odor control ducting shall not be applied to the primary façade of the building. (standard)

Managing Traffic During Construction: The Project Sponsor and construction contractor(s) shall coordinate with the Traffic Engineering and Transit Divisions of the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA), the Poli ce Department, the Fire Department, the Planning Department, and other construction contractor(s) for any concurrent nearby Projects to manage traffic congestion and pedestrian circulation effects during construction of the Project. For information about c ompliance, contact Code Enforcement, Planning Department at 628.652.7463, Monitoring - After Entitlement (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also r efer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of th is Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. Operation (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (A): The business operator shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. In addition, the operator shall be responsible for daily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance with Article 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed -source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passersby, appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liais on. filing_playbook.action: Contact San Francisco Planning by email to confirm in writing that adding beer and wine service qualifies as continuation of use under Planning Code Sections 810.44 and 178, and does not require a new Conditional Use Authorization.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that you operate an existing restaurant at 667 Commercial St that has been legally established since at least 1998 (Planning approval MA9900405) and 2014 (MB1400941), and you wish to add ABC Type 41 beer and wine service. Ask whether this is treated as continuation of the existing conditional use or as an intensification requiring a new CUA hearing. Reference comparable approvals at 653 Commercial St (Type 47 approved as continuation, case 2017-013358MIS) and 653 Clay St (Type 41 approved as continuation, case 2020-010940MIS). Request a written determination or a pre-application meeting to confirm the pathway before filing ABC or health applications.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: File for or renew the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate and the Health Permit to Operate through the SF Department of Public Health online portal, confirming continuation of the existing restaurant use.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the restaurant use at 667 Commercial St continues, and that beer and wine service is being added under an ABC Type 41 application. DPH will route the health permit application to Planning for a zoning referral; Planning should approve it administratively as continuation of use if step 1 confirmed that pathway. Attach the ABC application receipt, the certified food safety manager certificate, and proof of workers' compensation insurance. The health permit referral typically takes 14–45 days for administrative approval.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Enroll all alcohol-serving staff and managers in ABC-approved Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) training within 60 days of hire, and post the certification list on site for ABC inspections.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register each employee on the ABC RBS Portal ($3 per person), complete an approved RBS course (about $10–$25 per person), and pass the exam. Download the certificates and keep a current list of certified staff on the premises.

timeline_cost.notes: Timeline of 60–210 days and cost of $1,470–$2,600 are for approvals when granted, covering the Conditional Use Authorization (if required) and the Health Permit to Operate. ABC Type 41 application: 60–120 days per the permit catalog if unprotested; one to three months longer if census tract 611.01's undue concentration requires a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the city. Health permit to operate: 14–45 days per the catalog entry. The timeline assumes Planning confirms continuation of use; if Planning requires a new Conditional Use Authorization, add 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 per catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization, based on the one CUA comparable at 838 Grant Ave that took 183 days from filing to approval. Government fees: ABC Type 41 application $1,000–$1,600, health permit to operate $470–$1,000 (2026–27 schedule). Not included: San Francisco Business Registration Certificate $55–$700 (prerequisite, typically $55–$95 for a small restaurant), California Seller's Permit (free), EDD employer registration (free), RBS training $13–$55 per employee, ASCAP and BMI music licenses $600–$5,000 combined (not government fees), and any building permit if a change of occupancy is determined. The pending Miscellaneous Permit 2022-011138MIS filed November 14, 2022 at this address may affect the timeline; verify its status with Planning before filing.

records_summary: 667 Commercial St is in the CCB (Chinatown Community Business District) zoning district where restaurants are a conditional use on the first story. The records show this address has operated as a restaurant since at least 1998, with Planning approvals in 1998 and 2014 confirming continuation of the restaurant use. The immediate area is extremely dense with food and beverage establishments: 32 registered food/drink businesses and 14 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet. The base rate within 1,000 feet shows only 7 dated Planning decisions in the last 5 years (1 approved, 3 approved with conditions, 3 withdrawn, 0 denied)—too few to calculate an approval rate—but all restaurant applications in the CCB district on this block have been approved as continuation of existing uses or as permitted/conditional uses under Planning Code Section 810.
data_gaps: The pending November 2022 Miscellaneous Permit (2022-011138MIS) has no description in the records; cannot determine if it relates to the proposed alcohol service
ABC does not publish detailed conditions for existing licenses, so undue-concentration findings or operating restrictions at nearby licensed premises are not visible
No hearing transcripts or decision letters are available for the 1998 and 2014 approvals to show whether any conditions were imposed on the restaurant use
The site history shows 'limited restaurant' in 2014 and 'full-service restaurant' in 1998, but the current operating status and square footage are not documented in Planning records
Census tract undue-concentration data for ABC purposes is not provided; the 14 licenses within 500 feet is a proxy signal only
